game_identity_and_current_behavior.title: Beat Bug Blitz
game_identity_and_current_behavior.core_player_goal: Keep the health meter alive by dragging glitch bugs away from the central foot stage before they linger too long.
game_identity_and_current_behavior.fail_state: Health drains to zero when bugs stay on the stage too long, triggering the game over screen.
game_identity_and_current_behavior.success_score_state: Score increases by 100 per successfully tossed bug and the HUD displays the running clear count.
game_identity_and_current_behavior.camera_viewport_assumptions: Single full-screen fixed viewport with a canvas playfield and overlay HUD/screens.
game_identity_and_current_behavior.input_model: Mouse and touch dragging. Player presses on a bug, drags it a sufficient distance, and releases to clear it.
moment_to_moment_loop: Bugs spawn on the foot-shaped central play area.
Player selects a nearby bug with pointer or touch.
Dragged bugs visually lift upward with tweezers feedback.
If released far enough from origin, the bug is cleared and health recovers.
If ignored too long, bugs damage health continuously.
game_identity_and_current_behavior.current_progression: No explicit levels. Difficulty rises gradually through a continuously increasing difficulty scalar that speeds spawning and increases damage pressure.

mechanic_decomposition.description: Pointer/touch start selects a bug within radius, move drags it, end either clears it or snaps it back.
Bugs mostly stay in place with idle animation; dragged bugs follow pointer and gain visual lift.
Bugs spawn inside an ellipse over the foot at intervals that shorten as difficulty rises.
Selection uses radial hit testing; successful clear depends on drag distance from origin rather than collision physics.
Successful clear grants health recovery and 100 score; HUD reports clear count from score.
Any uncleared bug older than the grace period drains health, with stronger drain as difficulty rises.
There is no separate collectible type; bugs are both the threat and the removable target.
Start and game-over overlays wrap a single endless round with no discrete internal level transitions.
Top health bar, clear counter, reaction cards, start/game-over copy, and button labels explain state.
Canvas-drawn bugs, foot, particles, flash overlay, tweezers, vibration, and optional audio cues sell grabs, clears, and danger.
Audio infrastructure exists but media URLs are currently empty, so no active soundtrack or sfx are effectively integrated.

complexity_profile.overall_assessment: simple one-screen arcade with timing-heavy drag interaction and light continuous escalation
what_more_complex_should_mean_safely: Stronger world framing around the same drag-to-remove loop
Clearer staged fiction for the rising pressure
A conceptual five-level journey mapped onto the existing endless escalation
More expressive HUD language and visual progression, not new mechanical verbs
Optional safe tuning only if existing knobs are already exposed and do not change input semantics
avoid_for_complexity: adding combat spells with different inputs
changing the drag threshold or hit model significantly
rewriting the spawn system into lane logic
introducing menus, inventories, or projectile systems
replacing the canvas loop or physics behavior

protected_mechanics: bugs spawn on a central organic stage area
player clears targets by dragging them away and releasing
clear success is based on distance from the bug's origin
uncleared aged bugs drain health over time
score/clear accumulation and health recovery on successful clear
continuous endless-round loop with gradual difficulty increase
safe_theming_surfaces: start screen title, subtitle, and instructions
canvas-drawn bug silhouettes and color language
central stage/foot presentation reframed as another surface with the same shape role
background gradients, overlays, and ambient motion
procedural motifs around tweezers and bug glow
optional catalog-approved remote fonts or audio if later stages integrate them safely

remix_premise.title: Hogwarts Pest Control: Cornish Pixie Panic
remix_premise.world_premise: The player is a Hogwarts student in training, using enchanted golden tongs to remove cursed pixies and magical pests swarming a giant bewitched footprint map tied to castle ward stability.
recognizable_elements: Hogwarts house colors and castle silhouettes
owl post, candles, floating sparks, potion glow, and spell-circle motifs
magical creatures interpreted through the existing bug-removal loop
remix_premise.mechanic_fit: The drag action reads naturally as magically pinching and tossing pests off a warded training map. The health bar becomes ward integrity and the clear count becomes pests banished.
remix_premise.five_level_support: The premise scales through a journey from common room drill to castle corridors, greenhouse, Forbidden Forest edge, and final Great Hall ward crisis.
remix_premise.procedural_identity: Use code-native magical glyphs, castle windows, lanterns, house banners, potion vapors, star fields, and glowing pest silhouettes rather than pasted franchise stills.

level_1.title: First-Year Common Room Drill
level_1.definition: Base transformed experience. Player learns that enchanted pests landing on the ward map must be dragged off quickly to preserve ward integrity.
level_1.proof_of_scale: Shows the core loop with clear magical framing, readable pests, and house-themed UI.

level_1_5.title: Moving Staircase Mischief
level_1_5.definition: First meaningful escalation. The same drag-and-clear loop remains intact, but the scene gains stronger magical motion, more urgent copy, and slightly denser visual signals implying a broader castle outbreak.
level_1_5.proof_of_scale: Demonstrates that the same mechanics can feel like progression through world-state escalation, not new controls.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Common Room Practice
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Keep the training ward calm by flicking away pixies before they chew through the charm.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Safest, clearest onboarding expression of the existing loop.
safe_mechanics_knobs: Use base difficulty framing only if existing game already starts there
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: Small cursed pixies are the hazards; banished pests restore ward strength.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Do not clutter pests with too much detail that hurts hit readability.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Warm house banners, candlelight, and beginner spell glow.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Moving Staircase Rush
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Hold corridor wards together while roaming pests spill in between shifting castle passages.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: First escalation through stronger urgency and denser magical atmosphere.
safe_mechanics_knobs: Map to the game's natural early-mid difficulty curve
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: Pixies and cursed beetles represent mobile corridor chaos; each banish buys time.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Background motion must not camouflage pests.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Animated stair silhouettes and lantern sweeps.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Greenhouse Infestation
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Protect the herbology ward circle from a full magical pest bloom.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Represents the game's full intended mechanic stack in a richer environment.
safe_mechanics_knobs: Map to midgame spawn pressure already present
Use stronger feedback styling rather than new systems
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: Vine-lit pests crowd the ward; each removal restores protective magic.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Plant motifs should not obscure draggable entities.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Glowing glasshouse panes, drifting spores, emerald magic.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Forbidden Forest Edge
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Maintain the outer defensive sigil as darker creatures surge from the treeline.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Same mechanic stack under heightened pressure and darker tone.
safe_mechanics_knobs: Map to later natural difficulty curve already implemented
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: Shadowy pests feel more dangerous, but remain functionally identical draggable threats.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Low-light palette must preserve target contrast and mobile visibility.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Moonlit fog, antler-like branches, patronus-blue ward flashes.

five_level_difficulty_progression.title: Great Hall Night of 1,000 Charms
five_level_difficulty_progression.player_facing_goal: Survive the castle-wide magical outbreak and keep the grand protective seal alive.
five_level_difficulty_progression.difficulty_intent: Upper readable pressure while keeping inputs and readability stable.
safe_mechanics_knobs: Use the source game's highest natural pressure framing only
five_level_difficulty_progression.hazard_reward_interpretation: A storm of enchanted pests assaults the grand seal; every banish is a visible defensive win.
five_level_difficulty_progression.failure_risk_to_watch: Do not make the finale so bright or particle-heavy that it hides targets.
five_level_difficulty_progression.visual_progression_beat: Floating candles, shattered charm arcs, house-color magic converging.

primary_shapes: circles and ellipses for wards, seals, and glows
winged pest silhouettes built from ovals and triangles
procedural_art_system.character_silhouettes: Pixie-like magical pests remain small, circular-center creatures with wing/ear variations so target readability stays close to the source bugs.
procedural_art_system.item_silhouettes: Golden enchanted tongs replace stage tweezers cosmetically; particles become sparks, charm fragments, and rune motes.
procedural_art_system.icon_style: High-contrast magical glyph badges with thick outlines and glow halos.
background_layers: playfield-safe ward glow under the protected spawn area
animation_principles: slow ambient loops in the background
short reactive flashes for health danger and clears
motion should frame urgency without masking draggable targets
rely on opacity, scale, drift, and glow rather than complex transforms
implementation_preference: Canvas for reactive playfield art and pests
CSS gradients and overlays for screens/HUD
Optional inline SVG-like canvas motifs if helpful
DOM text overlays for tutorial and state copy
procedural_art_system.safe_fallback_if_external_assets_fail: Use entirely code-drawn glyphs, gradients, particles, and text styling with no dependency on external images.

stage_1_must_preserve_and_execute: Keep drag-to-remove mechanics, scoring, health drain, and endless loop intact
Re-theme copy, HUD labels, and canvas art to the Hogwarts pest-control premise
Prefer procedural wizarding motifs over asset-heavy replacements
Only use catalog-approved remote media if any remote media is added
stage_2_must_draw_build: Magical pest variants that preserve source readability
A ward-map replacement for the foot stage without changing spawn geometry role
Animated background layers for the five conceptual worlds
Harry Potter-inspired UI styling that avoids direct copyrighted still-image dependence
stage_3_must_refine: Feedback timing, color contrast, particle polish, and copy consistency
Visual escalation from level 1 through level 5 within the same mechanics
Mobile-safe HUD sizing and target clarity
stage_4_must_verify_and_repair: Gameplay still starts, drags, clears, and game-overs correctly
Readability remains strong on mobile viewport sizes
No thematic layer obscures pests or blocks pointer/touch action
Any added audio/media obeys catalog and runtime constraints
runtime_risks_to_watch: Overly ornate pest art shrinking the hit readability
Too many particles over the playfield
Changing the foot/stage geometry in a way that alters spawn comprehension
Introducing remote media without catalog approval
